articles.title: California’s killjoy bureaucracy is crushing the state’s rebel spirit and freedom
articles.summary: Steve Hilton proposes creating OFF, Office of Fun and Freedom, to slash California red tape blocking nightlife, block parties and more.
articles.body: California should be the most fun place in America. Look at what we have. Beaches, lakes, mountains, parks, incredible weather, great food and music, and people from every part of the world. It should be almost impossible to make California boring. But the politicians and bureaucrats who run our state are doing their best! CALIFORNIA PIZZA KITCHEN FOUNDER SAYS CALIFORNIA HAS BECOME TOO DIFFICULT FOR ENTREPRENEURS California was not built by killjoys. It became the world’s great magnet for artists, inventors, rebels and misfits because this was the place you came to create, experiment and live freely. Try doing something fun today. Want to put on a band at a small venue? You can end up dealing with separate rules for entertainment, dancing, sound, alcohol and zoning. Want to organize a block party? Get ready to deal with police, fire, health, public works and alcohol officials. Want to take your dog to the beach, gather your family around a firepit or turn a vacant storefront into a neighborhood meeting place? The answer from the killjoy bureaucrats: No, No, No. Or…maybe, but only once you’ve spent months — and thousands of dollars — proving that your harmless idea should be allowed. How did we get here? It wasn’t one law or one decision. The rules just piled up. Every time somebody identified a potential problem, the answer was another law, another regulation, another permit, form or ban. Nobody ever went back and asked whether the old rules still made sense. The bureaucracy only moves in one direction: more rules, more red tape, more infuriating, inhuman, joyless nonsense. More people telling you no. NEW YORK BUSINESS GROUP CAMPAIGNS TO END 'PROHIBITION-ERA' ALCOHOL RESTRICTIONS STATEWIDE Of course, we need rules against real harm. Nobody wants alcohol served to minors, unsafe food, wildfires, drunk driving or neighborhoods kept awake all night. But those are specific problems. Deal with them specifically. Instead, the killjoys use the possibility that something might go wrong as an excuse to stop everyone from doing anything. Big companies can hire lawyers and consultants. Independent venues, food vendors, musicians, nonprofits, families and volunteers simply give up. As governor, I will lead the fightback against the killjoys. I want to help restore the soul and spirit of California. That’s why as governor I will create OFF: a new Office of Fun and Freedom. OFF will be a small rapid-action team inside the Governor’s Office. It will not be another sprawling department. Its job will be to get rid of rules, not write new ones. LOS ANGELES NEIGHBORHOOD FOURTH OF JULY PARADE CANCELED AFTER BASS BUDGET CUTS, ORGANIZERS CLAIM In its first 100 days, OFF will audit state rules affecting nightlife, community events, food pop-ups, public recreation and social spaces. Every agency will have to explain what specific harm each restriction prevents. If it can’t, we’ll get rid of it. OFF will create one online front door for state event permits. Agencies will coordinate with each other instead of maddeningly sending people from pillar to post. Routine applications will have firm deadlines, with automatic approval if bureaucrats take too long. Californians will be able to see how long permits take, what they cost and which agencies are holding people up. We will name and shame the bureaucratic killjoys. And we’ll tackle the everyday rules that drive people mad. BAN ON BACKYARD BARBECUES ON CERTAIN DAYS IN CALIFORNIA FLOATED AS OTHERS PUSH BACK HARD A small bar, restaurant or coffee shop should not need a stack of approvals to host a band or let people dance. A volunteer organizing a block party should deal with one application and one deadline, not go on a scavenger hunt through government offices. Local communities should be able to create late-night zones where qualified venues stay open later, with plans for security, noise and safe rides home. California currently imposes a statewide 2 a.m. cutoff. Why should state politicians decide what works for every neighborhood, town, city? We should open more state beaches to dogs and provide more designated places for beach fires and family cookouts. Protect wildlife. Require leashes and cleanup. Close fire rings when the danger is high. But stop making a permanent ban the automatic answer to every risk. The same common sense applies to cannabis. California legalized it. Yet in too many places the result is the smell of weed in parks, on sidewalks and in other public spaces. Give adults legal places to use legal cannabis indoors, in age-restricted, properly ventilated licensed lounges. Local communities can decide whether to allow them. None of this is trivial. The stupid killjoy rules we have today are emptying downtowns, killing independent businesses and stopping people from spending time together. We spend enough of our lives isolated and stuck to screens. The government should make it easier to get together, not harder. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION California does not need another government office telling people what they cannot do. It needs one whose job is to get the killjoy bureaucrats out of the way. OFF – the Office of Fun and Freedom – will answer the call from Californians up and down our state: Leave us alone to have fun with our friends and families! Leave us alone to enjoy our beautiful state! Leave us alone, to be free! CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP It is time to restore the rebel spirit of California.

articles.title: Aaditya Thackeray, Rhea Chakraborty named in  Disha Salian's death case: Key details from CBI FIR
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday registered an FIR in connection with the death of Disha Salian, the former manager of l.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday registered an FIR in connection with the death of Disha Salian, the former manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput, following an order of the Bombay high court.The FIR names several individuals whose roles have been listed for investigation, including Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray, Rohan Roy, actors Dino Morea and Sooraj Pancholi, Aaditya's bodyguards, Rhea Chakraborty, Showik Chakraborty, former police officer Sachin Vaze, former Mumbai police commissioner Param Bir Singh, DCP Vishal Thakur and former Maharashtra chief minister Uddhav Thackeray.The document also names former state home minister Anil Deshmukh, several police officers, forensic officials, doctors and other individuals.“The then chief minister Uddhav Thackeray, father of Aaditya Thackeray, and others also played a significant role in the conspiracy and subsequent cover-up. The concerned public servants and police officers are also liable to be investigated for destruction or suppression of case papers, files and other public records, fabrication of official records, and misuse of public funds, manpower and police machinery for unlawful purposes and for shielding the offenders,” the FIR stated.The FIR said the listed individuals would be investigated in connection with the alleged principal offences, criminal conspiracy, the “subsequent creation and propagation of the false suicide story” and the alleged suppression, destruction or fabrication of evidence.It also named officers associated with Malvani Police Station, doctors and staff involved in the post-mortem, officials of the Forensic Science Laboratory in Kalina, security guards of Regent Galaxy Building, members of the special investigation team and other unidentified persons.Bombay HC orders CBI probeEarlier this month, the Bombay high court ordered a CBI investigation into Salian’s death and criticised the Mumbai Police for failing to register an FIR for six years.The court observed that the police investigation “raises more questions than answers”. The bench also questioned the decision to treat the case only as an accidental death and pointed to “glaring discrepancies” in the investigation.Salian died on June 8, 2020, after falling from a residential building in Mumbai’s Malad area. Mumbai Police had registered an Accidental Death Report (ADR) in the case.Salian had briefly worked as Sushant's manager. The actor was found dead at his Bandra residence on June 14, 2020, six days after Salian’s death.The proximity of the two deaths triggered widespread speculation about a possible link, although the cases were investigated separately.Following the public uproar over Rajput’s death, the Maharashtra government ordered a CBI probe. The agency later submitted a closure report stating that Rajput had died by suicide. The report, however, is yet to be heard by the court concerned.Earlier, Salian’s father, Satish Salian, had accused Aaditya Thackeray and actor Dino Morea in connection with his daughter’s death.Speaking to ANI on Friday, Satish Salian said he had told investigators what he knew about the events surrounding his daughter's death and provided names of several individuals whom he wanted authorities to examine.“I stated the facts exactly as they were; I told them everything that happened to my daughter. I listed all the names: Aditya, Sooraj Pancholi, Dino Morea, and the bodyguards. They noted everything down. They said they would take action based on what I told them; the proceedings would begin in a few days,” he said.“The truth cannot be defeated. God stands where the truth is; that is why justice will be served,” he added. Mumbai Police had earlier maintained, after its inquiry, that Salian had died by suicide.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Yemen gov’t forces advance in Taiz as Houthis claim attack on Saudi Arabia
articles.summary: Yemeni government forces have advanced in western Taiz after successfully repelling a Houthi offensive.
articles.body:
Armed forces affiliated with Yemen’s internationally recognised government have retaken positions from the Houthis and are advancing in the southwestern Taiz province as clashes intensify.

Reporting from Taiz on Monday, Al Jazeera Arabic’s Yasser Hassan said forces loyal to the Saudi Arabia-backed Yemeni government advanced in western Taiz on Sunday after successfully repelling a Houthi offensive.

“This comes with the support of air strikes targeting Houthi gatherings. The air force continues to bomb the Houthis. On the west coast in Mocha, Dhubab, and their surroundings,” Hassan said, citing a source in government forces.

In a statement on Monday, the Houthis, also known as Ansar Allah (supporters of God), said they launched attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia using dozens of ballistic missiles and drones.

The group said the attacks targeted “military facilities and infrastructure, including aircraft hangars, radar installations, runways, ammunition depots and other targets at King Khalid airbase in Khamis Mushait”, Saudi Arabia.

It said the attacks were a response to a Saudi offensive, which involved more than 300 air strikes across Yemen over five days.

There was no immediate comment from Saudi Arabia on the Houthi claims.

On Sunday, the Saudi civil defence agency sent alerts for the city of Abha and the region around Khamis Mushait, but they were quickly lifted shortly afterwards.

Fighting in Yemen’s more than 10-year civil war reignited in July, threatening a United Nations-brokered truce that halted large-scale violence in 2022, after the Houthis declared a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia and began targeting its ships in the Red Sea.

The fighting soon spilled over beyond the country’s borders, with the Houthis carrying out air attacks on southern Saudi Arabia, including oil facilities. Dozens of people were wounded in those attacks.

Clashes in Yemen intensified last week after the Houthis captured parts of the country’s Red Sea coast, fortifying their hold on the Bab al-Mandeb strait, a key waterway which handles about 12 percent of global trade, including 11 percent of maritime oil and 8 percent of liquefied natural gas (LNG).

The waterway has been an economic lifeline for Saudi Arabia and its oil exports, as the Strait of Hormuz has been effectively blocked by Iranian forces since the United States and Israel launched their war on Iran in February.

The Houthis captured more strategic islands in the southern Red Sea, The Associated Press news agency reported on Monday, citing Yemeni government and Houthi officials.

Houthi fighters were deployed on the islands of Greater Hanish and Lesser Hanish about 86 nautical miles (160km) north of the Bab al-Mandeb, according to two government officials and a Houthi official, the AP reported.

Meanwhile, the International Organization for Migration said on Sunday the fighting in Yemen in recent weeks had displaced nearly 86,000 people.

It added that some of those displaced by the conflict were fleeing Yemen altogether, with more than 2,000 people reaching neighbouring country Djibouti.

articles.title: 17 NCPI MPs to join BJP soon: Rebel TMC MP Jagadish Chandra Barma Basunia's big 'Durga Puja claim

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Seventeen of the 20 MPs are likely to join the ruling Bhartiya Janata Party either before or after Durga Puja in October, rebel TMC leader and Cooch Behar MP Jagadish Chandra Barma Basunia claimed Monday.According to Basunia, the MPs have decided to make the switch together, which he said would ensure that they are not disqualified under the anti-defection law."We are 17 MPs going to the BJP together. Since more than two-thirds of the 20 members will be moving, the anti-defection law will not apply to us," Basunia said.The development comes nearly three months after 20 dissident TMC MPs announced their merger with the little-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) on June 14 and extended support to the ruling NDA.The anti-defection law requires at least two-thirds of members of a legislature party to agree to a merger to avoid disqualification. In the case of the 20-member NCPI group, the threshold is 14 MPs.Basunia said, however, that three of the 20 MPs from the minority community would not formally join the BJP, citing the political and administrative dynamics in their constituencies.He named Abu Taher Khan, Khalilur Rahaman and Yusuf Pathan, saying they would extend support to the NDA from outside."They will support the NDA, and may be given important responsibilities or portfolios," Basunia said.Basunia's claim comes days after he and his wife, TMC MLA Sangeeta Roy, faced protests on returning to their ancestral home in Sitai, Cooch Behar.Locals and BJP workers staged demonstrations against the couple amid criticism of Basunia's political shift. A TMC office near his residence was also allegedly set on fire during the unrest.Basunia has maintained that he has severed ties with the TMC and is now aligned with the NDA.The Mamata Banerjee-led party suffered a massive breakaway of Parliament and assembly strength after its stinging defeat in Bengal polls at the hands of the BJP. articles.title: At least one dead, 25 missing after boat carrying migrants sinks off Greece
articles.summary: At least 51 people rescued as search operation continues off the island of Gavnos near Crete.
articles.body:
One person has died, 25 are missing and 51 people have been rescued after a boat carrying migrants sank off a Greek island near Crete, according to the country’s coastguard.

“Fifty-one were picked up by two boats that were in the area,” a coastguard spokesman said on Monday.

He said survivors had reported that 77 people were on board when the boat went down near the island of Gavdos.

Search and rescue efforts were ongoing, with four ships, boats, Frontex aircraft and a coastguard helicopter operating in the area, Greece’s public broadcaster ERT News reported.

The 51 rescued people were due to be brought to Crete, “where the prescribed procedures will be followed”, ERT reported.

After arriving in Crete, undocumented migrants generally face immediate arrest and temporary confinement before being transferred to closed detention camps on the Greek mainland. Under Greek law, individuals are subject to extended administrative detention, severe penalties and fast-track deportation.

Strong winds blowing through the area have been hampering the search operation, ERT said.

Crete and Gavdos, about 320km (200 miles) from the Libyan coast, have become the main point of entry for asylum seekers in Greece.

In late August, Greece’s ANA news agency published figures from the Ministry of Migration and Asylum that indicated that migrant arrivals in the country fell from about 61,000 in the year to August 2025 to 42,000 in the following 12 months – a decline of about 31 percent.

Greece’s conservative government in July suspended all asylum claims for migrants arriving by sea from North Africa for three months, a move it argued helped deter crossings.

The ban passed in parliament amid a surge in asylum seekers reaching Crete and after talks with Libya’s Benghazi-based government to stem the flow were cancelled in July.

The government remains at odds with regional authorities in Crete over a plan to build a permanent transit facility on the island. It is preparing draft legislation that would mandate imprisonment for people whose asylum claims are denied and require ankle monitors during a 30-day compliance period before deportation.

Authorities in Europe have tightened their immigration rules over recent years as far-right, anti-immigrant political parties have won increasing support throughout the continent.

Greece has been in discussions with Germany and several other European Union countries on setting up “return hubs” outside the bloc for processing migrants’ claims.

articles.title: 1 of 5 rescued baby orangutan develops fever at Odisha's Nandankanan Zoo, expert cites stress
articles.summary: BHUBANESWAR: One of the five baby orangutans rescued from a forest in Odisha and quarantined at Nandankanan Zoological Park since September 8 has deve.
articles.body: BHUBANESWAR: One of the five baby orangutans rescued from a forest in Odisha and quarantined at Nandankanan Zoological Park since September 8 has developed fever, prompting veterinarians to keep the animal under close medical observation.The other four orangutans are healthy and responding normally, officials said.One of the babies has been recording a high body temperature since Sunday and is being given medicines to control the fever, official sources said.Veterinarians are monitoring its condition closely and providing round-the-clock care, news agency PTI reported."One of the orangutans has had a fever since the day it was brought here. The fever subsides when given medicine, but reappears again. But it is now stable and under strict medical supervision," a senior official said.The quarantine enclosure at the zoo has recently become relatively crowded following the arrival of 58 new animals. However, officials said separate arrangements have been made for the five orangutans."We have made separate arrangements for the orangutans," the official said, adding that special mosquito nets have been installed in their temperature-controlled room.Experts cite stress, environment changeExperts said the fever could be linked to stress, fatigue or the sudden change in environment. The orangutans, which are not native to India, normally live in a rainforest environment and could take time to adjust to their new surroundings."It will take some time for the babies to get acclimated to the prevailing environment. The orangutans normally live in rainforest atmosphere," the veterinary officer said.According to Aditya Acharya, head of the Centre for Wildlife Health at Odisha University of Agriculture and Technology (OUAT), high body temperature in orangutans is monitored in a manner similar to that in humans."Normally, animals like human beings are administered paracetamol-based medication during high body temperature," Acharya said.He said the orangutan with high body temperature is also being given less food than usual.Odisha forms 5-member care panelThe Odisha government has constituted a five-member technical committee to oversee the care and upkeep of the five baby orangutans.According to an order, the panel will assess issues concerning the welfare and upkeep of the rescued animals and provide technical inputs for their proper care.It can also consult or co-opt experts and organisations of national and international repute whenever required.Chief Wildlife Warden and PCCF (Wildlife) PK Jha said three caretakers and doctors had been deployed round-the-clock to monitor the health of the babies.Jha, however, said he was not aware of one of the orangutans suffering from fever.He said the caretakers were taking proper care of the animals and feeding them every two hours as advised by animal health experts.The babies are being given milk every two hours, along with apple and banana fluids and boiled potatoes at regular intervals, according to a dietary chart prepared by experts.The orangutans have also been provided soft toys and swings and are made to listen to music to help keep them stress-free, officials said.Rescue and wildlife smuggling probeThe five baby orangutans were rescued from Bichitrapur forest in Bhograi block of Balasore district on September 8 and brought to the quarantine facility at Nandankanan Zoo the same night.Meanwhile, the Odisha Police's Special Task Force (STF) and the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) have intensified their articles.title: In January 2024, a homeless man played piano at a church in UK on a freezing night; 2 years after his video went viral, he has raised $50,000 for charity and found a home
articles.summary: UK News: In January 2024, homeless man Rhys Wynne-Jones walked into St. Mary’s Church in Penzance, England, on a freezing night and asked if he could play its .
articles.body: In January 2024, homeless man Rhys Wynne-Jones walked into St. Mary’s Church in Penzance, England, on a freezing night and asked if he could play its piano. His performance of Queen’s “Bohemian Rhapsody” was recorded by a volunteer and posted on Facebook. The video quickly went viral, changing the course of his life.Wynne-Jones, who had been homeless for about a decade, had gone to the church looking for shelter, Good news network reported. St. Mary’s is one of Britain’s ‘Night Churches’, which remain open around the clock for vulnerable people. After speaking to volunteers there, the 34-year-old asked if he could use the piano.Music had been a coping mechanism for him for years. As he started playing, volunteers and visitors gathered around to watch. For Wynne-Jones, the piano offered a way to quiet his thoughts during a difficult period in his life. “There is a lot of noise in my head, but when I play piano my head goes quiet, I feel calm,” he said.From church piano to charity gigsThe video soon attracted hundreds of comments from people who wanted to know who the young man known as the “Nightchurch Pianist” was. After Wynne-Jones came forward, his unexpected online attention led to more opportunities to play, including a special charity gig where he met British stars such as Ronnie Wood, Peter Andre and members of the cast of EastEnders.Wynne-Jones soon began using his music to support homeless charities and other good causes. He later collaborated with Peter Andre on a television pilot. He is also due to perform at a number of venues, including a theatre production in Bristol.Despite the attention, Wynne-Jones does not describe himself as a professional musician or celebrity. His focus remains on playing music and raising money for causes linked to homelessness.“I don’t see myself as a professional pianist or a celebrity figure. I only need enough money to cover my expenses,” he told SWNS news. “I just love to play the piano to raise money for homeless charities and good causes.”His performances have helped him raise more than £40,000 for charity, which is about $54,000.He now has a place to call homeOne of the biggest changes in Wynne-Jones’ life has been finding a permanent place to live. After years of homelessness, he moved into a new Coastline Housing development in west Cornwall.The new home has also given him a quieter place to continue playing music. He now practises on his Roland keyboard, while eating and sleeping in a safe place of his own.For Wynne-Jones, however, getting a home has not erased everything he experienced while living on the streets. He said, “the pain doesn’t end just because you’ve got a key”.His new life has nevertheless given him some calm. The memories of his time on the streets now motivate him to help and inspire other people.More than just a pianistWynne-Jones has also shown that his talents extend beyond playing the piano. As part of his act, he can recite all the countries of the world, the elements of the periodic table and the first 100 digits of the number Pi.His musical ability remains at the centre of his public appearances, but the attention surrounding him has also allowed him to connect with people in new ways. He has gained new followers on Instagram and uses those connections to encourage others.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Ammonia gas leak in Jordan’s Aqaba industrial area injures 11 people
articles.summary: State news channel, Al-Mamlaka, says the southern port of Aqaba was evacuated as a precaution.
articles.body:
At least 11 people have been injured in an ammonia gas leak in Jordan’s Aqaba industrial complex, local media reported.

The state news channel, Al-Mamlaka, reported on Monday that the southern port of Aqaba was evacuated as a precaution after the gas leak.

The commissioner for environment and public safety at the Aqaba Special Economic Zone ‌Authority, Nidal Al-Ouran, said the leak had been contained and that the injuries ranged from minor to moderate.

He said the incident occurred during maintenance work on an old pump or pressure equipment in the southern industrial ⁠area of Aqaba, away from residential ⁠areas. Ammonia gas that had accumulated in the equipment leaked in a small quantity, he said.

Without naming it, Al-Ouran said ⁠the maintenance work was being carried out for a Japanese company.

Workers ⁠would be allowed to ⁠return to their sites after teams from the authority and other relevant agencies carried out another inspection, took the necessary ‌measurements and confirmed there were no remaining risks, he said.

articles.title: New children's book festival in Stroud 'open to everyone'
articles.summary: Brimscombe Mill Kids Book Fest is offering free tickets to enable more children to come along.
articles.body:
A new book festival for children will be "open and accessible to everyone", regardless of whether they can afford a ticket, organisers say.

Brimscombe Mill Kids Book Fest will take place in Stroud from 9-10 October, with event tickets costing £4.50, although free tickets are available with "no judgement, no criteria", Jo Mansell from Brimscombe Mill said.

The festival will feature a secondhand bookshop, along with workshops and signings from local and national authors and illustrators such as Wren James, Alex T Smith, and Hannah Shaw.

Brimscombe Mill operates a pay-as-you-can restaurant, which will offer book-themed food during the festival, including the Bruce Bogtrotter cake from Matilda.

Mansell said: "We've created this [festival] amongst all of our normal values that we have at Brimscombe Mill, which is to make it open and accessible to everyone.

The festival will also include free table tennis tables, crafts, and a scavenger hunt.

But Mansell hopes Book Fest will also be accessible to readers of all levels of dedication, whether they "spend every night reading, or just want to come down and hear an exciting magic show".

The festival coincides with the National Year of Reading, and Shaw, author of the Unipiggle the Unicorn Pig series, said finding ten minutes in the day to read to children "makes such a difference".

"Obviously that's a lot of pressure for parents and I think it's just when you can fit it in," Shaw said.

"So even if it's not at bedtime, if it's five minutes before they go to school... it's just a really nice thing to do and get them off screens."

Alice Hodge from Stroud is one parent who bought tickets for her children to attend an event at Book Fest.

"I bought two tickets for my two sons, I have paid for them but I did notice there was an option you could make a lesser donation or pay nothing at all," she said.

Hodge said she does not often take her children to similar festivals, "but when it's so accessible, I'll definitely make the effort".

articles.title: Ukraine's top prosecutor leaves country, accuses rivals of corruption
articles.summary: Ukrainian Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko left the country overnight, media reported, just a few days after submitting his resignation in connection wit...
articles.body:
Ukrainian Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko leaves the country amid corruption scandal allegations against anti-corruption authorities.

Kravchenko accuses NABU chief of forging official documents for unlawful advantages, calls for heads of anti-corruption agencies to resign.

President Zelensky announces support for Kravchenko's dismissal, vote scheduled in parliament following ongoing investigations.

Ukrainian Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko left the country overnight, media reported, just a few days after submitting his resignation in connection with a corruption scandal.

He is reported to have left for Poland. On Monday, he levelled accusations against Ukraine's anti-corruption authorities, calling on their heads to resign.

Investigations have been launched against the head of the anti-corruption agency NABU, Kravchenko said in a video posted on social media.

He alleged that NABU chief Semen Kryvonos had forged official documents to gain huge unlawful advantages. Kravchenko also spoke of further investigations into another agency tasked with combating corruption.

Kravchenko said that he was on a "business trip" abroad. The Centre for Combating Corruption, a non-governmental organization, alleged that President Volodymyr Zelensky had allowed him to leave the country despite the ongoing investigations.

Officially, Kravchenko is still the prosecutor general - a vote on his dismissal is due to take place in parliament.

Zelensky responded 50 minutes after the publication of Kravchenko's video.

"There is only one path for this prosecutor general: dismissal from office. That is exactly what I told him," Zelensky wrote on Telegram. He called on lawmakers to support the dismissal. The vote has now been announced for Tuesday.

Despite half a dozen anti-corruption agencies being established since 2014 with Western assistance, Ukraine is regarded by experts at the Transparency International advocacy group as one of the most corrupt countries in Europe.

The Eastern European country has been defending itself against a Russian invasion since February 2022 and is receiving billions in support from the West.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz talks postponed due to Yemen events, says Iran
articles.summary: Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei says Iran does not interfere in Yemeni affairs.
articles.body:
Iran says a planned meeting with officials from Gulf states to discuss the Strait of Hormuz has been postponed due to “events unfolding in Yemen”.

Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei, addressing a news conference on Monday, said Oman and Iran “have taken a joint decision aimed at arriving at a responsible” approach to the management of the strait.

He said the meeting, scheduled to take place in Oman, would have been an “opportunity to demonstrate the significance of these decisions”.

“Had this meeting took place, it would have been a very suitable opportunity [to discuss the new policy]. I do not believe any responsible country would accept in any shape, way, or form to be dictated to or be subjected to pressure from any outside forces,” he said.

The Strait of Hormuz, which falls in Iran and Oman’s territorial waters, has been effectively blocked by Tehran amid the US-Israel war on the country.

Baghaei said Iran has “no relations whatsoever with what is unfolding in Yemen”, adding Tehran does not interfere in its affairs. He added that Saudi Arabia requested the postponement of the meeting.

Tensions between Saudi Arabia and Yemen have escalated since July, when Houthis, who control large parts of Yemen, declared a naval blockade on their northwestern neighbour. Clashes escalated last week as Houthis seized the port of Mocha, tightening their control over the Bab al-Mandeb strait.

Meanwhile, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Monday that its forces had intercepted and destroyed an advanced MQ-1 drone over the Strait of Hormuz.

In a statement carried by the semi-official Tasnim news agency, the IRGC said it intercepted the drone using a new aerospace defence system.

Regarding an attack on an Iranian commercial vessel on Sunday that killed one person, Baghaei said two Pakistani citizens working on board were also injured.

The United States and Israel “continue to target security” in the Gulf, he added.

articles.title: US says it’s clearing Hormuz traffic: Why are oil futures beyond $100?
articles.summary: Brent crude crosses $107 as Hormuz disruptions and Saudi pipeline shutdown threaten global oil supply.
articles.body:
President Donald Trump says the United States is making progress in reopening the Strait of Hormuz and escorting more oil through the waterway, yet oil prices have jumped in recent days.

The recent attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure have also pushed crude prices up, with Brent crude rising $3.21 to $107.82 a barrel.

The apparent contradiction between US claims and surging oil prices shows the reality on the ground is complicated at best.

So, what do we know about shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, and where are oil prices headed?

What are the US, Iran and others claiming about the Strait of Hormuz?

Washington says traffic through Hormuz has been improving despite the two sides being in a diplomatic deadlock.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright on Sunday said 10 million barrels of oil per day, on average over the past week, were passing through Hormuz, adding that “we’re back to two-thirds or north of two-thirds of the previous flows.

“So the world oil markets are tighter than we’d like today, but they’re not overly tight,” Wright added, according to US media outlet Bloomberg News.

President Trump has made similar claims, stating that the US is in “total control” of the strait and asserting that its forces are escorting ships carrying millions of barrels of oil through the waterway, through which a fifth of global oil and gas passes.

Iran has, however, disputed the US claims. Tehran says it controls access to Hormuz and has warned ships against using routes it has not authorised. Last week, Iran announced a new restricted shipping zone around the crucial waterway.

Shipping data from tanker trackers also suggests traffic remains well below normal levels. Preliminary ship-tracking data shows vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz falling to single digits a day over the weekend, remaining well below the 10-day average of 14 a day, the Reuters news agency reported.

Reuters said a total of 14 vessels transited the waterway, with four exiting the Gulf and 10 entering it.

More than 100 vessels passed through the strait daily, carrying an estimated 20 million barrels of oil, before the US and Israel launched the war on Iran in February.

The data is preliminary and subject to updates, as some vessels navigate the passage with their Automatic Identification System transponders switched off, meaning they are excluded from the official counts, Reuters added.

Oil prices jumped more than 3 percent on Monday after an Iranian ship was attacked on Sunday in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi Arabia’s critical East-West oil pipeline was damaged in a drone attack.

Brent crude rose $3.21 to $107.82 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate gained $3.17 to $103.22.

The rise came after Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline was temporarily shut by a drone attack originating from Iraq, according to Saudi officials.

Riyadh has been using the pipeline to export oil via the Red Sea amid the Iranian blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. Four percent of the global oil supply will be threatened if the pipeline remains shut.

A series of missile and drone attacks by Yemen’s Houthi group on southern Saudi Arabia in recent days has further added to the uncertainty about oil supply originating from the world’s largest oil producer.

On Tuesday, the Yemeni group hit civilian and economic sites in the cities of Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jizan and Najran, injuring 73 people, among them women and children.

The assault on the kingdom marks a sharp escalation in Yemen’s long-running war, which flared up again in July after nearly four years of relative calm under a United Nations-brokered truce.

Why are oil prices climbing, despite US assurances?

Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at IG Group, says oil prices are likely to remain under upward pressure as disruption in the Strait of Hormuz continues, despite US claims that it is clearing traffic through the waterway.

“Despite US claims to the contrary, Hormuz is not under its control, and oil is not flowing freely,” he said.

Beauchamp says passage through Hormuz remains severely limited and ships continue to face attacks, while Houthi attacks on infrastructure have added another source of concern for energy markets.

“Near-month futures continue to trade at a premium to the spot price, a recognition that disruption is expected to continue, ratcheting up the pressure on the global economy,” he added.

Christopher Haines, the Global Head of Oil, Energy Aspects, says crude prices will continue to rise, pointing out that oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz are still notably lower than pre-conflict levels and the global oil reserves, which helped steady the market over the last six months, have dwindled.

“The US Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) has little to give with announced releases having ended… while China will not be able to reduce their buying as they did in the summer due to higher seasonal demand in the winter,” Haines told Al Jazeera.

“Crude buying has been robust as refiners have to run harder to produce the fuels the northern hemisphere needs for heating.

“We believe oil prices can continue to rise, as without the buffers we have had over recent months, prices will have to increase to curb demand.”

Early on Sunday, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations centre said a vessel was struck by an unknown projectile while transiting Hormuz.

Meanwhile, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on Monday said it had intercepted and destroyed an advanced MQ-1 drone that was flying over the Strait of Hormuz.

“With no one in a hurry to talk, it seems that oil prices will continue to rise, and a return to March’s highs seems to be a matter of when, not if,” Beauchamp said.

A meeting in Oman between Gulf countries and Iran to discuss possible agreements on the Strait of Hormuz, which had been scheduled for Monday, was postponed, further delivering a blow to diplomatic overtures to end the six-month war.

Iran on Monday said the planned meeting was postponed by Saudi Arabia over the recent events in Yemen.

US Energy Secretary Wright also poured water over any hopes for a diplomatic breakthrough, saying “counting on a consensual agreement with Iran today is certainly not a good bet,” according to Bloomberg.

Meanwhile, Abdul Khalique, head of the Liverpool John Moores University Maritime Centre, said the Houthi group’s growing presence along Yemen’s western coast, next to the Bab al-Mandeb strait, was also a reason for a surge in oil prices.

“The Bab al-Mandeb strait is now largely under Houthi control,” Khalique told Al Jazeera, referring to the vital shipping route connecting Asia with Europe.

“Having already taken the port of Mocha and the islands of Hanish and Zuqar earlier in the week, Iran-aligned Houthi forces seized the strategically vital Perim (Mayyun) Island and the mainland town of Dhubab, giving them effective control of Yemen’s entire Red Sea coastline.”

Khalique added that war risk insurance for Hormuz transits, which stood at about 0.25 percent of hull value before the war, has climbed as high as 3 to 10 percent of hull value, depending on the vessel and route.

“For a $100m tanker, that range translates to a war risk premium of $3m to $10m for a single transit, before cargo cover and freight costs are added on top,” he said.

“The US may hold substantial military control over the battlespace, but it has not restored the conditions needed for a resumption of normal commercial shipping, and that gap is precisely why oil prices continue to climb even as Washington declares victory.”

articles.body: Dire warnings about AI shock Congress, but action is unlikely before the midterms. Oil prices rise and diesel hits a new high after a weekend of attacks in Iran. And why female athletes are speaking out against Sydney Sweeney’s new advertisement. Here’s what to know today. Congressional action on AI is unlikely before Election Day Stark warnings about AI systems are setting off fresh alarm bells on Capitol Hill, with Democrats and even some Republicans saying Congress must act quickly. However, it’s unlikely lawmakers will do anything before Election Day to address the dangers. Congress still has not passed any comprehensive legislation to rein in or create guardrails for AI, nor is there any consensus about how to tackle the issue. This is Morning Rundown, a weekday newsletter to start your day. Sign up here to get it in your inbox. Reps. House GOP leaders have also shown no urgency in prioritizing more sweeping regulations. Here’s what to know during the chamber’s final week in session before the midterms. It’s about the culture we’re creating for the next generation of girls in sports.” Read what other athletes said. articles.title: Megan Basham vs Pooja Sethi on viral photo of Texas university students: People are angry because this was not organic
articles.summary: US News: It all started with a photo of college sports fans at the University of Texas at Austin, but after it was mislabeled as the UT graduation photo by Bo .
articles.body: It all started with a photo of college sports fans at the University of Texas at Austin, but after it was mislabeled as the UT graduation photo by Bo French, a Republican, all hell broke loose as people did not like the presence of South Asians. It was later debunked that the photo was not from the UT graduation event, but then social media users were not ready to accept the presence of South Asians at any event of a Texas university.“I heard UT graduation this year looked like this,” Bo French wrote. “I didn’t believe it. The problem is now obviously far worse than anyone imagined.”French faced backlash from his own party for the open racism but the fallout of the entire episode was bigger.'This is what Texas looks like'Democratic nominee for Texas House District 47 in the 2026 election Pooja Sethi resisted French's racism and said Texas looks diverse. "If you look at a crowd of diverse Texas students celebrating together and see a “problem,” the problem isn’t the students. This is what Texas looks like. And if you don’t like it, you can leave," Sethi wrote and was asked to leave the US by America First activists.Author Megan Basham chose to confront Sethi and said that the students' ethnicity was not the problem. "The problem isn’t the ethnicity of the students. The problem is WHY the demographics of Texas universities have changed so drastically in the last 15 years. And the answer is largely because of the massive expansion of H1B visas. That is why people are angry. Because this was not organic," Basham said.Who is Bo French?Bo French is running for the state Railroad Commission and has a history of making anti-Muslim, antisemitic and anti-immigrant comments. He faced criticism last year after sharing a poll on social media asking who was the “bigger threat” to America, Muslims or Jews.Why Texas is often at the centre of America's immigration and culture warsTexas has become one of the most prominent battlegrounds in America's increasingly heated debates over immigration, demographic change and national identity. The state has one of the country's largest immigrant populations and is home to major immigrant communities from Mexico, India, Vietnam, China and other parts of the world. At the same time, Texas has remained firmly Republican at the state level, creating a political environment where immigration and demographic change are frequently debated through a conservative lens.Texas is also a major centre of the US technology and energy industries. Cities such as Austin, Dallas, Houston and San Antonio have attracted highly skilled workers from across the world. Indian professionals, in particular, have become increasingly visible in Texas's technology, healthcare and business sectors, while Indian students and families have established large communities around major cities and universities.That visibility has sometimes made the Indian-American community a target in broader arguments about immigration and the H-1B visa programme. Critics of the programme argue that companies rely too heavily on foreign workers, while supporters say skilled immigrants have become an important part of the US technology economy.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: China's spy chief flags AI threat, warns of 'cognitive warfare' & threats to national security
articles.summary: China News: China’s ministry of state security has issued its first public warning on the national security risks posed by artificial intelligence, accusing hosti.
articles.body: China’s ministry of state security has issued its first public warning on the national security risks posed by artificial intelligence, accusing hostile forces of using generative AI to spread political rumours, manipulate public opinion and threaten the country’s critical infrastructure.Minister of state security Chen Yixin said foreign actors were exploiting emerging AI tools to conduct what he described as public opinion and cognitive warfare against China.“Hostile forces and people with ulterior motives are abusing generative AI technologies such as deepfake audio and video, AI-generated text and images, and ‘intelligent troll armies’ to cheaply and on a mass scale fabricate political rumours, disseminate harmful information and incite divisive sentiments,” Chen wrote in an article published online on Sunday.“These activities constitute an attack on public opinion wars and cognitive warfare against China, directly threatening our political security, institutional security and ideological security,” he added.The MISS said AI could also create vulnerabilities for China’s cyber defences, sensitive data and military systems. Chen described the technology as “the main battleground for global technological competition and a new track for major power strategic rivalry”.He specifically cited the hacking capabilities of Anthropic’s Claude Mythos and OpenAI’s ChatGPT-5.5-Cyber, warning that such systems could “pose serious risks to China's critical information infrastructure”.Chen also accused foreign intelligence agencies of using AI-enabled tools to gather sensitive information.“Foreign intelligence agencies are deeply using technologies such as intelligent web crawlers, intelligent data mining, and intelligent profiling analysis to extensively collect and acquire sensitive information such as key national data, trade secrets, and citizens' personal privacy,” he said.The warning comes as Beijing and Washington prepare for discussions on AI governance. US president Donald Trump and Chinese president Xi Jinping are expected to discuss the issue at a meeting planned for September 24.The statement also follows growing concern among US technology executives over the pace of AI development. Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei has called for the industry to “slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models”, with OpenAI chief Sam Altman and Elon Musk backing the proposal. In a lengthy essay published on Saturday, he warned that a “Chinese lead in AI would pose grave danger for the United States and the world.”China’s foreign ministry rejected calls for confrontation over AI. Spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Monday, “Fearmongering, confrontation and vicious competition will only disrupt the process of global AI governance which serves no one's interest.”Chen, meanwhile, said China must “ensure independent control of key core technologies”, including advanced computer chips needed to train AI models.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Drenching rains bring flash flooding across coastal Connecticut, New York and New Jersey
articles.summary: WESTPORT, Conn. — Flash flooding from heavy rains prompted road closures, water rescues and commuter rail problems across the tristate area Sunday.
articles.body: WESTPORT, Conn. — Flash flooding from heavy rains prompted road closures, water rescues and commuter rail problems across the tristate area Sunday. The National Weather Service said the hardest-hit areas appeared to be northern New Jersey, parts of New York’s Westchester County and a swath of coastal Connecticut along Interstate 95. The service issued flash flood warnings across the region for much of the morning Sunday as rain fell at a rate of 1 to 2 inches (2.5 to 5 centimeters) an hour in places. Metro-North and Amtrak said their rail lines to New Haven, which serve Norwalk, Bridgeport and other major Connecticut communities, were experiencing delays and cancellations due to flooding impacts. Tweed New Haven Airport also closed its departures terminal due to local flash flooding. Airport officials in a Facebook post said travelers with flights departing Sunday should not come until further notice. Connecticut Gov. Ned Lamont and other state officials, meanwhile, urged drivers to avoid flooded roadways and not to attempt to drive through standing water. Water rescues conducted in Connecticut coastal cities The coastal stretch from Norwalk to Westport was among the most impacted in the state, receiving 6 to 7 inches (15 to 18 centimeters) of rain Sunday morning, with rainfall rates reaching 3 to 4 inches (8 to 10 centimeters) per hour. In Westport, emergency responders conducted 13 rescues of people trapped in vehicles by floodwaters, according to the fire department. Photos and videos shared on social media showed downtown businesses inundated. “Even as the rain subsides, standing water and other hazards may remain,” the department cautioned on Facebook. “Residents should continue to avoid flooded roads, never drive around barricades, and give emergency crews room to work.” In Bridgeport, the fire department said in a social media post it answered “call after call” on Sunday, including deploying boats “to rescue residents from flooded areas and bring them to safety.” Photos shared by the department showed residents being helped into a boat from the door of a house, with rescuers standing in knee-deep water outside. The heavy rains also forced multiple road closures and some water rescues in White Plains and other major communities in New York’s Westchester County. In New Jersey, Paterson Mayor Andre Sayegh said emergency crews rescued about 20 people from rapidly rising floodwaters, including a woman who fell out of her wheelchair and ended up floating in the street. Sayegh said there were no immediate reports of any deaths or severe injuries from the deluge, even as video shared on social media showed parked cars submerged nearly up to their windows on some roads. As the rains tapered off and the skies cleared, Paterson’s annual Dominican parade stepped off Sunday afternoon, though with a slight delay.

articles.title: King Charles to host major AI leaders amid growing warnings over threat to humanity
articles.summary: UK News: King Charles III invites leading AI executives to discuss governance and ethical standards amid growing concerns over advanced technologies potentially endangering humanity. Join the conversation on AI's role in society and the need for regulation.
articles.body: Britain’s King Charles III will host top leaders of the global artificial intelligence industry this week for crucial talks on whether shared principles are needed to govern the rapidly advancing technology.The meeting at Dumfries House, Scotland, comes as warnings over AI’s potential threat to humanity grow louder. Executives from Nvidia, Google DeepMind, OpenAI and Anthropic, along with the UK’s minister for AI, are expected to attend.The talks follow warnings from two Anthropic researchers that increasingly powerful AI systems could eventually lead to the extinction of the human race. Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei also said on Saturday that AI companies should slow the pace of developing new models.The concerns come as AI systems are being used for increasingly sophisticated tasks, including by people carrying out criminal or harmful activities. Anthropic said in a threat intelligence report last week that its Claude models had been used in weapons development, cyber operations, surveillance and fraud.Finding a common approach among major AI powers could prove difficult. US President Donald Trump rejected calls for a slowdown in AI development on Sunday, while China's state-backed Global Times newspaper accused Anthropic of using a “Cold War playbook” against Beijing.Buckingham Palace said the discussions would focus on how AI could be used to benefit society while protecting human dignity and contributing to the “flourishing of both people and the planet”.Charles has previously used his position to bring leaders together to discuss major global issues. As Prince of Wales and later as king, he has particularly focused on environmental challenges and the role of business in addressing them.Britain has taken a relatively light-touch approach to AI regulation, positioning itself closer to the United States than the European Union.The country is also home to a growing AI industry and is a leading European destination for AI funding and startups. Its AI Security Institute, established after the 2023 AI Safety Summit, has voluntary agreements with major technology companies that provide access to their models before deployment.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Woman shocked by Aldi's AI response to dip complaint
articles.summary: Jo Reeves complained after finding hairs in her dip and the Aldi response included an AI prompt.
articles.body:
A woman who found hairs in her Aldi dip has said she was disappointed the company included an AI prompt in its reply when she complained.

Jo Reeves from Cotteridge in Birmingham said she found the "vile" hairs when she popped out for a snack, while her partner was in hospital.

The AI prompt included the phrase: "Make it short and concise but do not overdo it" and Reeves said: "Everyone uses AI but the language is disappointing as a customer.

An Aldi spokesperson said: "This response fell well below our normal standards of customer service. We have contacted Ms Reeves directly to apologise and fully resolve the issue she had with our product."

Reeves said: "My partner was having an op in Worcester hospital so popped to the local Aldi to get 'recovery food'."

She said she found the hairs while eating some Aldi chicken caesar loaded dip.

Speaking about the hairs, she said: "We were disgusted and put them in the bin.

"I can kind of excuse one hair, sort of, but two..."

The full Aldi response did give Reeves some advice on how to get a refund and told her "we're taking your feedback seriously" but did not include an apology.

It was the use of AI which annoyed her though.

Reeves said: "They might very well have written: 'Send an email to a customer who is making a mountain out of molehill, give the bare minimum and keep them sweet'."

She said she accepted human errors occured, but added: "I'd like to question their authenticity.

"They always present themselves from a marketing and customer services perspective as genuine and authentic. Yet, this is their reply. Disappointing."

articles.title: Grisly discovery from legendary Roman emperor's reign reveals soldiers' remains, weapons
articles.summary: A Roman military camp from the reign of Marcus Aurelius was unearthed near Šurany, Slovakia — with soldiers' skeletal remains, weapons and rare gate designs found at the site.
articles.body: An ancient Roman military camp tied to the era of a legendary emperor has been unearthed in Slovakia — complete with soldiers' remains, weapons and armor. The discovery, made near Šurany in western Slovakia, was announced by the Institute of Archaeology of the Slovak Academy of Sciences (SAS) earlier this summer. The excavation was conducted ahead of construction of an industrial park and covered roughly 370 acres. 1,740-YEAR-OLD ROMAN COIN BEARING EMPEROR'S NAME FOUND AS ENGLAND RAIL DIG REVEALS CLUES The second-century A.D. camp dates to the reign of Marcus Aurelius. It was likely used during the Marcomannic Wars, a series of bloody conflicts involving Germanic tribes along the Roman Empire's northern frontier. Aurelius, who ruled Rome from 161 to 180 A.D., is remembered as both a powerful emperor and Stoic philosopher whose writings were compiled into the influential work "Meditations." "The Šurany discovery follows the earlier identification of the first Roman camp in the Hron River region near Želiezovce, where it is believed that Emperor Marcus Aurelius wrote parts of his philosophical work Meditations," a statement noted. It is the first Roman military camp discovered in the Nitra region of Slovakia. Unlike similar Roman camps, the site "does not follow the typical rectangular layout," officials said. Instead, the camp has an unusual, irregular layout while still retaining the typical features associated with Roman marching camps. ANCIENT CLUE CRACKS OPEN A 2,000-YEAR-OLD MYSTERY NEAR FAMED COLOSSEUM "It contains all the characteristic defensive features of a Roman marching camp, including five entrance gates, fortifications, and a clavicula, a distinctive gate design featuring a curved ditch and rampart that forced attackers into a vulnerable approach," the release added. "This is the first time a clavicula gate has been identified in Slovakia." Archaeologists also found what officials described as "an extraordinary number" of human skeletal remains. Complete skeletons and scattered bones were found in storage pits, wells, shallow graves and defensive ditches. ANCIENT GOLD RING UNEARTHED AT GRAVE CARRIES 2,000-YEAR-OLD SECRET MESSAGE Although the camp appears to have been abandoned after a conflict between Roman and Germanic forces, the identities of the dead remain uncertain. Lead archaeologist Marek Vojteček said preliminary findings suggest many were Roman soldiers. "It fills an important gap in our understanding of Roman activities north of the Danube during the final third of the second century." "Alongside the skeletal remains, we uncovered numerous pieces of Roman military equipment, including spears, arrowheads, fragments of helmets, segmented and scale armor, legionary belt fittings, coins and the distinctive caligae military sandals, identified by the iron hobnails preserved in their soles," Vojteček said in the release. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "We also recovered everyday objects such as an axe, a knife and gaming dice." Research at the site will continue, with officials describing the excavation as a "long-term scientific process" that could take years to yield answers. In a statement, Matej Ruttkay, director of the Institute of Archaeology, said the discovery "has significance far beyond the borders of present-day Slovakia." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS "It fills an important gap in our understanding of Roman activities north of the Danube during the final third of the second century," he said. "The circumstances are also exceptional. We are investigating a site that appears to have been abandoned immediately after a military conflict between the Romans and the Germanic tribes, as demonstrated by numerous archaeological finds." Last year, archaeologists uncovered an ancient mass grave beneath a soccer field in Vienna containing the remains of as many as 150 people, believed to include Roman soldiers and Germanic tribesmen. articles.title: Why the Houthi advance towards Yemen’s Marib, Taiz matters
articles.summary: Marib is home to Yemen’s oil sector. Whoever controls it secures economic gains. Taiz’s location makes it critical.
articles.body:
Yemen’s government forces have carried out air attacks against the Iran-backed Houthis to repel their advances, as the rebel group has been gaining ground in government-held positions in the past week.

The focus of the fighting is now shifting to the region of Marib – the government’s last remaining stronghold in the north and a major oil and gas hub. Should the Houthis gain control of it, it could decisively turn the tide of the war in their favour, say analysts.

Heated battles are also taking place in western Taiz, on the western coast, where reports suggest government forces, supported by Saudi Arabia, are now on the counteroffensive after losing some ground there last week. A video released on Monday by the Yemeni army purports to show Houthi positions and vehicles being bombed there.

Trapped in the middle are the civilians. The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has reported that more than 85,000 have been forced to flee their homes since the beginning of September. More than 2,000 have fled into Djibouti’s northern shores.

It is the last remaining stronghold of anti-Houthi forces in northern Yemen. A Houthi expansion there would threaten government presence and weaken its leverage in the north.

Marib also hosts the country’s largest gas and oil fields, meaning that whoever controls it holds some of Yemen’s most important energy infrastructure and a potentially crucial source of revenue.

“Dominating Marib’s oil and gas resources has been a Houthi goal for more than a decade. Without facing a crushing defeat in Marib, they would keep fighting to achieve that goal,” Saddam al-Huraibi, a Yemeni political commentator, told Al Jazeera . Should they gain control of it, the group could earn great leverage to negotiate favourable terms in any future mediation effort.

A Houthi capture of Marib would be a “watershed moment” in terms of the country’s internal dynamics, said Adam Baron, a fellow at the Future Security Program of the New America think tank. Still, he said, it will be a tough fight as government forces will see this battle as an existential war. “Losing Marib would be an absolute crushing defeat” for the forces of Yemen’s internationally recognised government, he added.

Marib is also geographically significant because it lies on the easiest road that runs from northern Yemen to Shabwa Governorate in the south – a seafront on the Gulf of Aden and the Arabian Sea – and al-Mahra Governorate.

The optics of a win in Marib would also be a powerful propaganda tool for the Houthis, helping them convince many Yemenis that the group is on a roll militarily and is poised for even greater victories, said Nabil Hetari, a Yemeni writer and human rights activist.

There is also a humanitarian dimension. Over the years, the city has been welcoming displaced people from areas which have fallen under Houthi control since the fall of the capital Sanaa in 2014. According to IOM figures from 2023, Yemen recorded nearly 2.8 million internally displaced people, more than half of whom (58 percent) are in Marib.

“All the parties involved in the battle are focused on Marib as a potential decider in the nature of their exit from this war,” said Hetari.

The strategic importance of Taiz lies in its geography.

The governorate forms a bridge between the Houthi-held north and the government-held south and the Red Sea coast. Thus, whoever controls it gains the upper hand in the movement of weapons and supplies between the interior and the southern port city of Aden.

Taiz also carries considerable political weight. One of Yemen’s largest population centres, the city became an important centre of resistance to the Houthis after they seized Sanaa in 2014 and has endured years of fighting and restrictions on access. A major Houthi breakthrough there would therefore carry symbolic significance far beyond the territory captured.

Its western coast also stretches towards Mocha, a historic town that the Houthis captured last week, and towards the Bab al-Mandeb strait, a chokepoint connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.

Bab al-Mandeb is one of the world’s most important shipping routes. The 20km- (12-mile-)wide waterway lies between Yemen and Djibouti, connecting Europe to Asia. Before fighting resumed, about 12 percent of global trade passed through it. In recent days, the Houthis have grabbed most of Yemen’s Red Sea coast, including Mayyun (Perim) Island, which lies in the strait.

“The Houthis seek to move closer to this vital waterway to threaten maritime traffic. Such a move aims to keep the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb under the influence of Iran and use them as leverage against regional and international powers,” said Fuad Mussed, a Yemeni analyst and author. “This is a strategy Tehran has been pursuing for years.”

This is a serious concern for Saudi Arabia, which has been relying on the Red Sea route to export its oil, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: China rejects AI slowdown calls, blasts U.S. tech leaders’ ‘fearmongering’
articles.summary: Urgent calls for a slowdown in the development of artificial intelligence may cite a grave threat to humanity, but China says the warnings are instead aimed at slowing its progress as America’s rival superpower.
articles.body: HONG KONG — Urgent calls for a slowdown in the development of artificial intelligence may cite a grave threat to humanity, but China says the warnings are instead aimed at slowing its progress as America’s rival superpower. Beijing on Monday dismissed the intervention from U.S. tech leaders as “fearmongering” and part of a “Cold War playbook.” It’s the latest sign that competition between the two countries could outweigh mounting safety concerns, after President Donald Trump also rebuffed the warnings from industry leaders and said his focus was on beating China on AI. The comments followed a lengthy essay that was published Saturday by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and endorsed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX founder Elon Musk. Amodei said that companies should deliberately “slow the pace” at which they improve their models given the potential risks. He also said that a “Chinese lead in AI would pose grave danger for the United States and the world,” and called for the U.S. to restrict sales of key tech to China. That message was not welcomed by Beijing. “Fearmongering, confrontation and malicious competition will only disrupt the process of global AI governance and serve no one’s interests,” China’s foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters at a regular news briefing on Monday. The state-run Global Times newspaper had a more blunt tone on Sunday, blasting the call for an industry-wide slowdown as “packed with containment provisions targeting China and is, in essence, a ‘Cold War playbook’ for the AI sector.” AI has advanced at a breakneck speed, with models rapidly getting smarter, faster and cheaper. They have also frequently outpaced technical safeguards, fueling security fears. Those fears have now reached a crescendo, but also exposed just how far apart Beijing and Washington seem to be on cooperating to address them. Amodei himself likened the situation to the Cold War arms race, telling CBS’ ‘Sunday Morning’ that the two sides should work together, but that he didn’t hold out much hope. Altman, the head of OpenAI, similarly said on X late Sunday that “where we will need the help of our government is for international coordination.” But that might not be compatible with Trump’s approach. “We’re leading China in AI. We’re the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI wins,” the president told reporters Sunday. He criticized “very negative forces” for bringing up things “that won’t happen.” While Trump rebuffs safety concerns, Beijing has acknowledged AI security risks. State security minister Chen Yixin said Sunday that China must “accelerate the establishment of a system for preventing and controlling AI security risks.” Chen also said in the state-run China Cyberspace magazine that “we must engage extensively in international cooperation,” identifying AI as “a new track for strategic rivalry.” The difference in approach on tackling AI progress is likely to be a central issue when Xi and Trump meet on Sept. 24 in Washington. Amodei’s essay came just a few days after U.S. agencies published an alert saying that top China AI companies have systematically copied cutting-edge AI models from American companies. Beijing rejected this accusation its companies had been “distilling” U.S. models. China has also rejected any outside take on how its companies should pace development. “They want to write the rules. I don’t think they want to follow anybody else’s,” Ja Ian Chong, an associate professor of political science at the National University of Singapore and a nonresident scholar at Carnegie China, told NBC News in a phone interview. “There’s the sort of talk of cooperation, but the behavior suggests otherwise, and underlying that behavior, I think, is this deep mutual suspicion,” Chong said. Chinese companies now offer advanced AI performance at a fraction of the cost of U.S. models, with President Xi Jinping pitching China as a pioneer of open-source models in contrast to those produced by most leading American companies. At the BRICS summit in India on Sunday, he offered member nations help to develop open-source AI. Xi has also outlined a potential global governance framework on AI among the Global South. Chong said the distillation clash highlighted the suspicion toward China in both the White House and Silicon Valley. “It’s a bit like an arms race. And to get de-escalation there needs to be simultaneous neutral self restraint and it’s difficult to see how that would come about in this kind of environment,” said Chong. But not everyone is so pessimistic. While a U.S.-China agreement on curbing AI progress may be a long shot, the countries could separately pursue greater regulation, said Theo Bertram, director of the London-based Social Market Foundation. “The idea that we could see the domestic introduction of some safeguards in both countries is not impossible,” Bertram said in a phone interview. “You do it domestically and it’s in everyone’s interest to learn and share and for there to be accountability,” he said. “Some greater accountability is one way of trying to mitigate what is inevitably going to be a growing political and public demand globally.”

articles.title: Kejriwal-Sardesai Goa gambit: Attack defections, welcome rivals
articles.summary: India News: The Aam Aadmi Party and Goa Forward Party on Sunday announced a new political beginning for the state. They announced a pre-poll alliance for the upco.
articles.body: The Aam Aadmi Party and Goa Forward Party on Sunday announced a new political beginning for the state. They announced a pre-poll alliance for the upcoming 2027 assembly election named 'Goa First' and promised voters something the state has struggled to get: a mandate that actually stays intact.There was plenty of familiar political rhetoric at the launch in Panaji on Sunday. AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal claimed that BJP would not win a majority. "The people of Goa want a change. Goa First will form the government. We will win on our own," Kejriwal claimed.Both parties presented the alliance as a credible, "non-BJP, non-Congress alternative".In the press conference, the newly-formed alliance tried to build its political identity around a simple charge: defection.GFP chief Vijai Sardesai attacked the ruling establishment as a government of defectors. He said the BJP had not received a complete mandate in the previous elections and that even the Congress leadership could not deny the possibility of another round of defections.Kejriwal also opened up about the recent Rajya Sabha defection led by former blue-eyed boy Raghav Chadha. "It is a matter of great regret that our Rajya Sabha MPs left the party. They betrayed the party. The party sent them to the Rajya Sabha; the people did not send them," the AAP chief said.He said the AAP had never betrayed the people through its elected representatives."We believe that this is a lesson for us because such a thing has never happened in the Aam Aadmi Party before. From now onwards, before sending anyone to the Rajya Sabha, we will scrutinise the person thoroughly and ensure that he is the right person," Kejriwal said.However, after the story of 'Goa First' gets interesting, at its hard-launch itself.GFP chief Sardesai declared: "This alliance has not closed the door; it is open to the like-minded political forces. Many people have approached us, including leaders from both parties who are tired of their politics.Memory of 2017 and 2022The anti-defection pitch is not difficult to sell in Goa because voters have seen the numbers change dramatically after elections.In the 2017 assembly election, Congress emerged as the single-largest party with 17 of the 40 seats, while the BJP won 13. Yet Congress did not form the government. The BJP stitched together a coalition with regional parties and independents, with GFP chief Vijai Sardesai becoming deputy chief minister.Two years later, the picture changed again.In July 2019, 10 Congress MLAs joined BJP, taking the saffron party's strength to 27 and giving it a clear majority. The Congress, which had started the assembly term with 17 MLAs, was left with five.Then came the 2022 election.This time, BJP turned out to be the single largest party with 20 seats in the hung assembly. Congress won 11 and AAP two, while GFP won one. BJP formed the government with support from 2 independents and Maharashtrawadi Gomantak Party (MGP).Six months later, however, again eight of Congress's 11 MLAs joined BJP.Among them were former chief minister Digambar Kamat and then leader of opposition Michael Lobo. Congress was reduced to just three MLAs, while BJP's strength rose to 28.Defection runs so deep in Goa politics that, just eight months before the 2022 exodus, some Congress MLAs had gone to extraordinary lengths to prove they would stay put. They visited a temple, chapel and mosque, and signed affidavits promising not to defect. In September 2022, eight of the 11 Congress MLAs joined the BJP anyway.After years of battle in the assembly and courts, the Supreme Court in July had agreed to hear a plea challenging a decision of the Goa assembly speaker rejecting a petition by the Congress for disqualification of the eight MLAs.For Goa First, this history of defections may prove to be strong campaign material.The 'open door' politicsSardesai himself made clear that 'Goa First' is not going to be a closed club.The alliance, he said, was open to "like-minded political forces". He claimed that leaders from both major parties had already approached them because they were tired of their respective politics.Strategically, that makes perfect sense.AAP and GFP together currently have only three assembly seats. If the alliance wants to become a serious statewide force, it needs some established names and local networks. Goa's politics is intensely constituency-driven and established local faces can matter enormously.Turning away a strong BJP or Congress leader simply because that leader once belonged to the other camp could leave 'Goa First' with an admirable principle and a thin candidate list.But by welcoming such politicians, the alliance risks playing the very same game it accuses BJP of playing.However, if the leader joins before the elections, the alliance could defend it easily.The GFP complicationThere is another reason Sardesai's role makes this debate particularly interesting.GFP itself has travelled through Goa's shifting alliance landscape.In 2017, it was part of the BJP-led coalition that formed the government after Congress emerged as the largest party. By 2019, the relationship had broken down, and Sardesai became a bitter opponent of the BJP government. GFP subsequently allied with Congress for the 2022 election.It is now joining hands with AAP and positioning itself against both BJP and Congress for the 2027 elections. Thus, the positioning of the party has remained fluid.That, though, is not necessarily a contradiction, as we have seen several regional parties routinely negotiate their political space by switching alliances.The 'Goa First' alliance has now officially entered the 2027 Goa contest with defection as one of its central political themes. Yet, with its doors open to leaders from the BJP and Congress, the alliance's own composition could become part of the election narrative. The first real test of that balancing act will come with its candidate selection.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
